contract_plain_english: Finite volume methods represent q on a grid cell by its cell average: the integral of q over the whole cell divided by the cell's volume, rather than by a point value at a grid point.

source_evidence.anchor: Integral conservation law (1.10) and its following explanation
source_evidence.location: raw PDF page 26; printed Chapter 1 page 4
source_evidence.observation: The source treats the integral of q over an interval as the total amount of the conserved quantity, changed only by flux through the endpoints.

source_evidence.location: raw PDF page 27; printed Chapter 1 page 5
source_evidence.observation: The domain is divided into grid cells, and the method approximates the total integral of q over each cell, or actually the cell average of q, defined as that integral divided by the volume of the cell.

binders: A grid cell C with finite positive volume |C|.
A scalar- or vector-valued conserved-density field q that is integrable over C.
The cell average of q over C.
conclusions: The cell average over C is (1/|C|) times the integral of q over C.
Finite volume methods approximate this cell-integrated or cell-averaged quantity rather than a pointwise value at a grid point.
definitions_and_conventions: The total integral over C represents the cell's total conserved quantity.
The cell average is the cell integral divided by the volume of the cell.
For a vector q, integration and averaging are componentwise.
In the one-dimensional setting of Chapter 1, cell volume is the cell's length, though the prose uses the dimension-independent word 'volume'.
hypotheses: The computational domain is partitioned into grid cells.
The integral of q over C and the positive cell volume |C| are defined.
implicit_context: Finite-volume data is intended to remain meaningful when q has discontinuities, provided q is integrable.
The paragraph describes approximate numerical cell averages but gives no time index, grid index, quadrature rule, or reconstruction formula at this point.
A nonzero cell volume is implicit because the definition divides by that volume.

details: The integral is normalized by the full cell volume, not left as an unscaled total.
The stored finite-volume quantity represents an average over a cell rather than a point sample.
Cell integration matches the integral form of the conservation law that remains meaningful across discontinuities.

undebatable_constraints: A cell average is the integral of q over the entire grid cell divided by the volume of that cell.
The divisor must be the cell volume and must be nonzero.
The quantity is cell-based, not a pointwise approximation at a grid node.
The definition applies to the conserved-density field q and is componentwise when q is vector-valued.
The finite-volume motivation comes from the integral conservation law and its validity for discontinuous solutions.
